meta.updateStatus: Official API series refreshed; curated evidence unchanged
meta.scope: World, Europe / Netherlands, and selected-country comparisons

question: Are longer lives becoming healthier lives?

verdict.label: Longevity recovered; healthy years and care capacity do not move automatically with it
verdict.text: Global life expectancy has recovered above its 2019 level in the World Bank series. In 2023, Eurostat estimated 81.4 life-expectancy years but 63.1 healthy life years for the EU, and 81.9 versus 59.0 for the Netherlands under its activity-limitation definition.
verdict.direction: Life expectancy is recovering, but comparable healthy-life and system-performance trends are patchier.
verdict.distribution: Health, access and workforce capacity differ within and between countries.

questions: Who is benefiting or carrying the cost?
What evidence would change our current conclusion?

lifeExpectancy.label: Life expectancy at birth
lifeExpectancy.denominator: period life table for total population

healthyLifeYears.denominator: Period life table combined with self-reported activity limitation using Sullivan method
healthyLifeYears.caveat: Healthy life years are not WHO HALE. National implementation of the activity-limitation question can hamper cross-country comparison.

evidence.observation: In 2023, the EU age-standardised avoidable-mortality rate under age 75 was 237.7 per 100,000: 150.9 preventable and 86.8 treatable.
evidence.interpretation: Prevention and treatment contribute through different mechanisms and should remain separate.
evidence.caveat: Avoidable mortality uses agreed cause lists and an under-75 boundary; it is not every premature death.

evidence.observation: In 2024, 3.6% of EU residents aged 16 or older who needed medical examination or treatment reported unmet need due to cost, waiting lists or distance; 6.0% among people at risk of poverty versus 3.2% among others.
evidence.caveat: Self-reported unmet need combines three barriers and is not a clinical waiting-time measure.

evidence.observation: WHO's 2025 GLASS dashboard includes more than 23 million confirmed infection episodes reported by 110 reporting areas for 2016–2023.
evidence.interpretation: AMR surveillance has widened and can reveal resistance patterns.
evidence.caveat: Reported episodes and participation measure surveillance coverage, not a comparable global burden trend.

evidence.observation: Health accounts can separate preventive care from treatment and other functions.
evidence.interpretation: Spending shows resource allocation, not causal health benefit.
evidence.caveat: Definitions, prices, purchasing power, age structure and accounting differ; no spending-outcome causal claim is made here.

dataGaps: No single waiting-time definition is comparable across world, EU and national systems; this brief reports unmet need instead of manufacturing a league table.
Mental-health burden estimates depend on diagnostic coverage, survey instruments and disability weights; no mixed-definition trend is plotted.
Prevention spending is not treated as evidence that prevention caused an observed outcome.
Consumer wearables and speculative longevity interventions are excluded from outcome claims without defined clinical evidence.
rivalExplanations: Longer survival can coexist with more years lived with disability because mortality and morbidity change differently.
Apparent cross-country healthy-life gaps can partly reflect survey wording, reporting culture and institutional-population coverage.
Access can worsen despite higher staffing or spending when demand, case complexity, distribution and workflow change.
Pandemic recovery can lift life expectancy without proving a durable improvement in chronic or mental-health burden.
reversalIndicators: Healthy life years rise faster than life expectancy across repeated, definition-stable observations.
Preventable and treatable mortality fall across income groups and regions, not only in national averages.
Unmet need and definition-stable waits fall while safety and health outcomes hold or improve.
Workforce capacity, retention and geographic distribution improve together.
AMR incidence and resistance fall under stable testing and surveillance coverage.

possibilities.label: Hypothesis
possibilities.text: Better prevention may compress morbidity, but spending alone cannot demonstrate that pathway.

possibilities.label: Possibility
possibilities.text: Automation may release clinical time if workload, safety and access outcomes improve in real settings.

possibilities.label: Data gap
possibilities.text: No defensible global composite healthspan score joins outcomes, access, workforce and individual risks.

sources.institution: World Bank, sourced from UN Population Division and national statistics
sources.title: World Development Indicators: Life expectancy at birth
sources.geographyPopulation: World, Netherlands, Japan, United States; total populations
sources.interpretation: Tracks period life expectancy at birth.
sources.caveat: Does not measure healthy years, distribution within countries or care-system performance.

sources.institution: World Bank, sourced from World Health Organization workforce data
sources.title: World Development Indicators: Physicians
sources.geographyPopulation: World, Netherlands, Japan, United States; total populations
sources.caveat: Latest years differ; density does not measure distribution, workload, quality or access.

sources.title: Healthy life years by sex (hlth_hlye)
sources.denominatorUnit: Years at birth; life table plus activity-limitation prevalence
sources.interpretation: Shows that lifespan and years without activity limitation differ.
sources.caveat: Not WHO HALE; national question implementation can hamper comparisons.

sources.title: 1 million deaths from avoidable conditions in 2023
sources.interpretation: Separates public-health prevention from timely effective treatment.
sources.caveat: Categories overlap by agreed allocation and do not cover all premature mortality.

sources.title: 3.6% experience unmet needs for medical care in 2024
sources.geographyPopulation: EU residents aged 16+ who reported needing examination or treatment
sources.interpretation: Measures self-reported unmet need across cost, waits and distance.
sources.caveat: Not directly comparable to administrative waiting-time targets.

sources.title: Updated WHO dashboard offers new insights on antimicrobial resistance and use
sources.geographyPopulation: 141 participating countries, territories and areas; 110 reporting infection episodes
sources.denominatorUnit: Confirmed infection episodes and reporting areas
sources.interpretation: Documents scale and reach of surveillance.
sources.caveat: Coverage and testing intensity vary; counts are not burden rates.

sources.title: Health care expenditure (SHA 2011) metadata
sources.denominatorUnit: Expenditure classified by function, provider and financing scheme
sources.interpretation: Defines curative, rehabilitative, long-term and preventive care as separate spending functions.
sources.caveat: Accounting records allocation; it does not establish causal health outcomes.
